- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; reduce forecast peaks when sentiment is strong or trending up.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment; increase forecast lows when sentiment is negative or trending down.
- Avoid over-optimism after sharp price spikes; cap forecast overshoots by 5–10% relative to recent high.
- Mean-revert forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mixed, especially if price has deviated >15% from recent 7-day average.
- Adjust horizon-specific bias: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate in early cycles (e.g., post-spike) and underestimate in late cycles (e.g., post-downturn).
- Use sentiment as a momentum filter: if sentiment > 0.5, slightly reduce forecast slope; if sentiment < -0.3, slightly increase forecast slope.
- Correct for lag: if true outcome is significantly below forecast, check if sentiment was bullish 3–5 days prior — if so, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
